stem: Which of the following is system software?
explanation: System software manages the hardware and runs other programs; an operating system is the main example. Word processors, spreadsheets and games are application software used for user tasks.

stem: Which of the following is a web browser?
explanation: A web browser is a program used to view web pages, and Firefox is one. Excel is a spreadsheet, Windows Explorer manages files and Notepad is a text editor.

stem: A computer network that covers a single building or campus is called a:
explanation: A Local Area Network connects computers within a small area such as a building or campus. A WAN covers large regions and a MAN covers a city.

stem: Software that is designed to damage or disturb a computer system is called:
explanation: Malware is any malicious software, such as viruses and worms. Firmware is built into hardware, freeware is free to use and middleware connects software components.

stem: What does the abbreviation "WWW" stand for?
explanation: WWW is the World Wide Web, the collection of linked pages that are accessed over the internet using a browser.

stem: The name given to an unwanted bulk email message is:
explanation: Spam is unsolicited bulk email, usually advertising. Cookies are small files stored by websites, packets carry network data and a cache stores recently used data.

stem: Which of the following protocols is used to transfer web pages?
explanation: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) carries web pages between server and browser. SMTP and POP3 deal with email, and FTP transfers files.

stem: Which device connects different networks and forwards data packets between them?
explanation: A router reads the destination address of each packet and sends it toward the correct network. A hub merely repeats data to all ports and a repeater only boosts a weakening signal.

stem: Which network topology connects every device to a single central device?
explanation: In a star topology each node has its own link to a central hub or switch. A bus uses one shared cable, and a ring joins devices in a closed loop.

stem: What is the function of the Domain Name System (DNS)?
options: It encrypts the data sent over web pages
It converts domain names into IP addresses
It assigns hardware addresses to network cards
It blocks unwanted websites for the user
explanation: DNS works like a phone book that finds the IP address for a name such as example.com. It does not encrypt traffic, nor assign MAC addresses, nor act as a filter.

stem: A firewall is mainly used to:
options: Increase the free space on the hard disk
Speed up the main processor of the system
Remove dust from inside the computer case
Control incoming and outgoing network traffic
explanation: A firewall applies rules that allow or block network connections to protect a system. It has no effect on processor speed or disk capacity.

stem: Which type of malware replicates itself across a network without needing to attach to a host file?
explanation: A worm copies itself from computer to computer on its own. A Trojan pretends to be useful software and needs the user to run it, and spyware secretly collects information.

stem: Sending fake emails that trick users into giving passwords or bank details is called:
explanation: Phishing uses messages that look genuine to steal sensitive information. Spooling queues print jobs, booting starts the computer and formatting prepares a disk.

stem: Which software manages files, memory and running programs on a computer?
explanation: The operating system allocates memory, schedules programs and organises files. A compiler translates code, antivirus detects malware and a database stores data for applications.

stem: A software that checks files for known malicious code and removes it is called:
explanation: Antivirus programs scan for signatures and suspicious behaviour of malware. A device driver lets the OS talk to hardware and formatters only prepare disks.

stem: Which of the following describes a URL?
options: The address of a web page on the internet
A type of malicious program that spreads by email
A unit used to measure computer memory
A language used to write computer programs
explanation: A Uniform Resource Locator gives the location of a resource, such as https://www.example.com/page. It is not malware, a memory unit or a language.

stem: Which of the following passwords is the strongest?
explanation: A strong password is long and mixes upper and lower case letters, digits and symbols that are not a dictionary word. The other choices are common and easy to guess.

stem: A device that converts digital signals to analogue signals for transmission over a telephone line, and back, is a:
explanation: A modem modulates and demodulates signals. A switch connects devices in a LAN, and a scanner and plotter are peripheral devices.

stem: Which of these addresses uniquely identifies the network card in a device on a local network?
explanation: A MAC address is assigned to the network interface hardware. An IP address may change with the network and a domain name is a text name. A port identifies a service on a device.

stem: Which of the following is true about a switch in a LAN?
options: It sends every packet to all connected devices
It converts domain names into addresses
It sends data only to the intended device
explanation: A switch learns which device is on each port and forwards frames only there. A hub is the device that sends to all ports.

stem: A virus that attaches itself to the boot sector of a disk is called a:
explanation: A boot sector virus infects the first sector that the computer reads when starting. A macro virus infects documents that contain macros.

stem: What does the "https" at the start of a web address indicate?
options: The website contains no advertisements at all
The connection between the browser and website is encrypted
The website is stored on the local computer
The website is run by a government office
explanation: HTTPS adds encryption (TLS) to HTTP so data cannot be easily read by others. It says nothing about adverts or who owns the site.

stem: In a bus topology, what happens if the main cable breaks?
options: Nothing, because data uses another route
The network is split or fails
explanation: All devices on a bus share one backbone cable, so a break stops communication across it. The other topologies, such as a mesh, offer alternative paths.

stem: Which protocol is mainly used to send email from a client to a mail server?
explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends outgoing mail. POP3 or IMAP are used to receive it, FTP transfers files and DNS resolves names.

stem: The internet is best described as:
options: A single very large computer in one country
A type of application software for offices
A program that is used only for typing
explanation: The internet connects millions of networks globally using common protocols. It is not one computer or one program.

stem: Which type of network is the internet?
explanation: The internet spans the whole world, so it is a very large WAN. A LAN or PAN covers a small area, and an intranet is a private network.

stem: Which of the following best describes a Trojan horse?
options: A program that repeats itself across a network by itself
A program that appears useful but hides harmful code
A backup copy of an operating system
explanation: A Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users into running it. The self-copying program described in the second option is a worm.

stem: Which of the following does the term "bandwidth" refer to?
options: The physical width of a computer monitor
The total length of a network cable
The size of the keys on a keyboard
The amount of data that can be transmitted per second
explanation: Bandwidth is the capacity of a connection, measured in bits per second. It is not a physical dimension.

stem: Which of the following is used to protect data during transmission by converting it into unreadable form?
explanation: Encryption scrambles data so only someone with the key can read it. Compression reduces size and defragmentation reorganises a disk.

stem: What is special about open-source software?
options: It can be used only for a short trial period
It is always written by a government
Its source code is available to study, change and share under its licence
It has no licence and no conditions at all
explanation: Open-source software makes its source code available and its licence allows people to modify and share it. A trial period describes shareware, and open-source software still comes with a licence.

stem: At the sending computer, data moves down through the OSI layers. After it leaves the Presentation layer, which layer does it reach next?
explanation: Top to bottom the order is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical, so after Presentation comes Session. Application is above Presentation, so data has already passed through it.

stem: In asynchronous transmission, each 8-bit character is sent with 1 start bit and 1 stop bit. How many bits in total are sent for 100 characters?
explanation: Each character takes 8 + 1 + 1 = 10 bits, so 100 characters take 100 x 10 = 1000 bits. 800 counts only the data bits and forgets the start and stop bits.

stem: To which IPv4 address class does the address 172.20.5.9 belong?
explanation: The class depends on the first number: Class B covers 128 to 191, and 172 lies in that range. Class C starts at 192.

stem: Software that can be used free for a trial period, after which the user is expected to pay to keep using it, is called:
explanation: Shareware is 'try before you buy' software. Freeware is free to use with no payment expected at any time.

stem: A torch (flashlight) app asks for permission to read the user's contacts and track her location at all times. What is the main concern?
options: Copyright, as it copies the user's photos
Plagiarism, as it uses another app's name
Privacy, as it collects personal data it does not need
Piracy, as the app is free to download
explanation: A torch app needs no contacts or location, so collecting them is a privacy risk. Being free to download does not make an app pirated.

stem: Asad receives an e-mail saying his bank account is blocked and asking him to click a link and log in. What is the safest action?
options: Do not click; contact the bank through its official website or helpline
Click the link quickly before the account closes
Reply with his account number to ask for help
Forward the e-mail to friends to warn them, then log in
explanation: Urgent messages with login links are a common phishing trick, so he should check through the bank's own official contact details. Clicking the link or replying with details gives the attacker what he wants.

stem: A signal repeats every 0.02 seconds. What is its frequency?
explanation: Frequency = 1 / period = 1 / 0.02 = 50 cycles per second, that is 50 Hz. 0.02 Hz wrongly takes the period itself as the frequency.

stem: A student keeps sending threatening and insulting messages to a classmate on social media. This behaviour is called:
explanation: Cyberbullying is using digital media to repeatedly threaten, insult or harass someone. Phishing is tricking people into revealing personal details.

stem: At which OSI layer does a router mainly work?
explanation: A router routes packets between networks using IP addresses, which is the job of the Network layer. A switch works at the Data Link layer.

stem: A carrier wave keeps the same amplitude and frequency, but its phase is shifted to carry the data. This is:
explanation: Changing the phase (position in the cycle) of the carrier is phase modulation. Amplitude and frequency modulation change the strength and the rate of the wave.

stem: Counting the Physical layer as layer 1, which OSI layer is layer 3?
explanation: From the bottom: 1 Physical, 2 Data Link, 3 Network, 4 Transport. The Transport layer is layer 4, one above.

stem: A shop buys one licensed copy of a program and installs it on 20 computers, although the licence allows only one. This is:
explanation: Installing software beyond what the licence allows is software piracy, which breaks copyright. Paying for one copy does not give the right to make 19 more.

stem: Kamran must leave his office computer for a few minutes while he is logged in. What is the safest thing to do?
options: Lock the screen so a password is needed
Leave it open, since he will return soon
Write his password on a note beside it
Turn off the antivirus to save power
explanation: Locking the screen stops others using his logged-in account while he is away. Leaving it open, even briefly, lets anyone act in his name.

stem: Zara shares a group project document. Two members only need to read it. Which permission should she give them?
explanation: Giving people only the access they need (view only) protects the document from accidental or unwanted changes. Edit rights are unnecessary for people who only read.

stem: Which statement correctly describes a digital signal?
options: It has a limited number of separate values, such as 0 and 1
It changes smoothly and can take any value in a range
It can be carried only by radio waves
It always has a higher frequency than an analogue signal
explanation: A digital signal jumps between discrete levels that stand for bits. A signal that varies smoothly over a continuous range is analogue.

stem: How many layers does the OSI reference model have?
explanation: The OSI model has seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation and Application.

stem: Students in a city have fast Internet at home, while students in a remote village have no connection at all. This difference is an example of:
explanation: Unequal access to the Internet between places, such as city and village, is a classic case of the digital divide. Algorithmic bias is about unfair results from computer systems.

stem: An office has a wired LAN. Staff want their laptops and phones to join this LAN by Wi-Fi. Which device should be connected to the LAN?
explanation: A wireless access point lets Wi-Fi devices join a wired network. A hub or repeater only works with the wired signals and gives no wireless link.

stem: A cable run in a factory is so long that the signal becomes too weak to read at the far end. Which device regenerates the signal so the cable can be extended?
explanation: A repeater receives a weakened signal and regenerates it at full strength. A modem converts between digital and analogue signals and does not exist to extend a cable.

stem: In which topology is each device connected to exactly two neighbouring devices so that the links form a closed loop?
explanation: A ring joins each device to the next and the last back to the first, making a loop where every device has two neighbours. A bus is an open line with two ends, not a loop.

stem: In a star network, the cable between one computer and the central switch is cut. What is the effect?
options: All the computers lose their Internet link
Only that computer loses its connection
Every other computer slows down by half
explanation: Each computer in a star has its own cable to the centre, so a cut cable isolates only that computer. The whole star stops only if the central switch or hub itself fails.

stem: IPv6 was introduced mainly because IPv4 addresses were running out. How long is an IPv6 address?
explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits, written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits. 32 bits is IPv4, and 48 bits is the length of a MAC address.

stem: A company's logo and brand name are legally protected as a:
explanation: A trademark protects names, logos and symbols that identify a business. A patent protects a new invention.

stem: In which modulation is the amplitude (strength) of the carrier wave changed according to the data, while its frequency stays the same?
explanation: AM varies the height (amplitude) of the carrier to carry data. FM keeps the amplitude fixed and changes the frequency.

stem: Which hardware component must a computer have to connect to a network?
explanation: A NIC (network adapter, wired or wireless) connects the computer to the network medium. A graphics card drives the display and a sound card handles audio.

stem: A student guesses a teacher's password, logs into the school's result system and changes his own marks. What has he done?
options: Used the system in a fair way
Only broken a rule of netiquette
Gained unauthorised access, a computer crime
Made a lawful backup of the data
explanation: Entering a system with someone else's password and changing data without permission is unauthorised access (hacking), a crime. It is far more serious than a lapse in online manners.

stem: With a walkie-talkie, both people can talk, but only one at a time while the other listens. This is which transmission mode?
explanation: Half-duplex allows both directions, but only one direction at a time. Full-duplex would let both talk at the same moment.

stem: In online messages, writing whole sentences in CAPITAL LETTERS is considered poor netiquette because it:
explanation: Netiquette (online manners) treats all-capital text as shouting, which is rude. It has nothing to do with storage or viruses.

stem: The word 'modem' is formed from which two words?
explanation: Modem stands for modulator-demodulator: it modulates digital data onto an analogue signal to send and demodulates it on receiving.

stem: A bank wants data to keep flowing between its main servers even if any one link between them fails. Which topology best meets this need?
explanation: In a mesh each device has several paths to the others, so data can take another route when one link fails. A star depends on its central device, a bus on its single backbone, and a simple ring breaks when one link fails.

stem: Which list puts the network types in order from the smallest area covered to the largest?
explanation: A LAN covers a building or campus, a MAN covers a city and a WAN covers countries or the world. Putting MAN before LAN swaps the two smaller types.

stem: A student scans a paid e-book and shares the PDF with his whole class group so nobody needs to buy it. This is:
options: Fair sharing of public domain work
Legal because it is for studying
Allowed because the book was bought once
explanation: Copying and distributing a whole paid book without the owner's permission breaks copyright. Buying one copy gives the right to read it, not to give copies to everyone.

stem: Which computer stores the files of a website and sends a page to a browser when it is requested?
explanation: A web server holds the site's files and answers browser requests with pages. The browser is the program on the user's side that asks for and displays them.

stem: In fibre-optic cable, data is carried as:
explanation: Fibre-optic cable carries light pulses through thin strands of glass or plastic. Electrical current in copper is how twisted-pair and coaxial cables work.

stem: A school computer lab has 30 PCs in one room, each joined by its own cable to one switch. This is best described as a:
explanation: One room is a small area, so it is a LAN, and every PC having its own cable to a central switch is a star. A bus would use a single shared cable instead of separate cables.

stem: A tuition centre's online sign-up form must collect only what it needs to enrol and contact students. Which set of fields best follows this privacy practice?
options: Name, class, phone and bank card number
Name, class, phone and home Wi-Fi password
Name, phone and every social media password
explanation: Good privacy practice is to collect only the personal data needed for the purpose; name, class and phone are enough to enrol and contact a student. Card numbers and passwords are sensitive and not needed here.

stem: A Caesar cipher replaces each letter with the letter 3 places later in the alphabet (A becomes D). How is the word BAT encrypted?
explanation: B+3 = E, A+3 = D, T+3 = W, giving EDW. YXQ shifts each letter 3 places back instead of forward, and CBU shifts by only 1.

stem: When software is installed, the user is asked to accept a legal agreement stating how it may be used. This is the:
explanation: The licence agreement (often called the EULA) sets out the user's rights and limits, such as how many computers it may be installed on. Accepting it is a legal step, not a violation.

stem: An engineer invents a new type of machine and wants the legal right to stop others making and selling it. What should she obtain?
explanation: A patent protects an invention and gives the inventor the right to stop others making or selling it for a period. A trademark protects only a brand name or logo.

stem: A full mesh network connects 6 computers so that every computer has its own dedicated link to every other computer. How many links are needed?
explanation: A full mesh of n devices needs n(n-1)/2 links: 6 x 5 / 2 = 15. The answer 30 counts every link twice, once from each end.

stem: A face-recognition system was trained mostly on photos of light-skinned faces and makes more mistakes with darker-skinned faces. What is the main cause?
options: A virus in the camera software
Too many users at the same time
explanation: When training data does not represent all groups, the system learns patterns that work poorly for the missing groups; this is bias in computing. A slow connection would not make errors depend on skin colour.

stem: A desktop PC has no network port and no Wi-Fi. What must be fitted to it so that it can join the office Wi-Fi network?
explanation: Each computer needs its own network interface; for Wi-Fi this is a wireless NIC. A repeater or hub is a separate network device and gives the PC no network interface of its own.

stem: The first octet of an IPv4 address is (11000000)₂. To which class does the address belong?
explanation: (11000000)₂ = 128 + 64 = 192, and Class C covers first octets 192 to 223. Class B ends at 191, so 192 is the first Class C value, not Class B.
